messages:
maria: Heads up — token-level latency dashboard spiking for /v1/generate between 12:03–12:12 UTC after yesterday's runtime roll. P99 up to ~1.2s per token.

metrics-bot: ALERT: inference.token_latency_ms.p99 > 1000ms for route=/v1/generate (detected 1749001229)

kevin: I see the per-route KPIs too. Also seeing dropped OTLP metrics in the collector logs around the same time. Could be exporter queue overflow.

jess: FYI otel-collector.log shows: 'dropped 34k metrics in 9m due to full_queue' — root cause looks like a sudden spike in cardinality from route_tag=request_id.

liam: Can you paste the exact log snippet?

jess: ```
2025-11-01T12:05:18Z otel-collector exporter.go:312 INFO dropped_metrics=1234 reason=full_queue target=clickhouse
2025-11-01T12:07:45Z otel-collector exporter.go:312 INFO dropped_metrics=9876 reason=full_queue target=clickhouse
2025-11-01T12:10:01Z otel-collector exporter.go:312 INFO dropped_metrics=23123 reason=full_queue target=clickhouse
```

maria: Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.company/d/abcd/token-latency — breakdown shows queue+kv-cache wait dominating; compute time looks normal.

kevin: Query I ran in analytics: `sum by(stage) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))` -> stage=queue ~0.8s, stage=kv_cache_wait ~0.15s, stage=compute ~0.25s. So most of the p99 is waiting prior to compute.

tara: We did change StatsD batching defaults in the last deploy (reduced buffer to speed flush). That could lower headroom on the exporter side. Also saw some missing metrics for certain routes in StatsD sink.

liam: Proposed immediate actions: 1) bump OTEL exporter queue_size to 20000, 2) sanitize route_tag to remove request_id/high-cardinality values (routing.sanitizer), 3) run metrics backfill for the window where drops occurred.

maria: How do we run the backfill safely? Docs?

kevin: Backfill is `python tools/backfill_metrics.py --from 2025-11-01T12:00Z --to 2025-11-01T12:15Z --route /v1/generate --mode idempotent` — runs on analytics-runner and writes deduplicated aggregates to ClickHouse. Important: use `--mode idempotent` to avoid double-counting. Also ensures token-level breakdowns are restored.

jess: I just opened a quick PR to the otel collector to drop request_id from resource/metric labels: https://git.redwood/infr/otel/+/1234 — should land after a quick config review.

maria: :thumbsup: Can someone kick the backfill and watch dashboards? I want to see p99 move back down.

liam: Kicking the backfill now on analytics-runner. Start time 1749001300. Watching CPU and clickhouse ingest.

metrics-bot: JOB STARTED: metrics-backfill-20251101-1200 (id=mf-20251101-01)

liam: Backfill complete — rehydrated ~34k metric points for /v1/generate window. Dashboards show P99 down to ~120ms now. KV wait reduced after cache tweak.

tara: Filed INF-567 to tune StatsD exporter defaults and add an alert: otel.dropped_metrics > 1000 over 10m. Assigned to infra team.

maria: Great work — leaving a follow-up to infra to finalize exporter defaults and add automated backfill playbook to runbook. Adding notes to oncall.

kevin: Follow-up items: add sampling/scrubbing in statsd pipeline, increase exporter buffers, and add a short-lived high-cardinality detector that alerts before collector queue fills.

jess: I'll monitor after the config deploy lands. If we see any further drops I'll trigger the backfill playbook we just exercised.

maria: Thanks everyone — feel free to add anything I missed.
